questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

He said that he was booking a hotel room.
options_en: He said, "I am booking a hotel room."
He said, "He is booking a hotel room."
He said, "I was booking a hotel room."
He says, "I am booking a hotel room."
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Continuous Tense.

Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Present Continuous (Subject + is/am/are + V1 +ing + Object)

For example:

He said that he was checking the assignment. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I am checking the assignment." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

He- I

Was - am

So, the sentence in direct speech is: He said, "I am booking a hotel room."

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

She told her friends that she would be moving to a different state because she had accepted a job offer that required her to relocate.
options_en: She said to her friends, "I would have been moving to a different state because I had to accepted a job offer that requires me to relocate."
She said to her friends, "I was been moving to a different state because I have accepted a job offer that requires me to relocate."
She said to her friends, "I will be moving to a different state because I had have been accepted a job offer that requires me to relocate."
She said to her friends, "I will be moving to a different state because I have accepted a job offer that requires me to relocate."
questions.solution_en:
The initial part sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Present Conditional Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Future Simple Tense.

Present Conditional (Subject + would/should + V1 + object) will be converted into Future Simple (Subject + will/shall + V1 + object).

For example:

He said that he would go to Kolkata on Friday. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I will go to Kolkata on Friday" (Direct Speech)

For latter part-

Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object) will be converted into Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

Followed by the end part-

Simple Past (Subject + V2 + Object) will be converted into Simple Present (Subject + V1/V5 + Object).

For example:

He said that he wanted a new job. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I want a new job." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

"would be" changes to "will be".

"Told" changes to "said to".

"she" changes to "I"

"Her" changes to "me"

"Had" changes to "have"

"Required" changes to "requires"

Therefore, the correct answer is: "She said to her friends, "I will be moving to a different state because I have accepted a job offer that requires me to relocate.""

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.q_en:
In the following question, a sentence is given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives choose the one which best expresses the sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.

The stranger said to me, "Please help me as I am lost."
options_en: The stranger requested me to help him as he is lost.
The stranger requested me to help him as he has lost.
The stranger requested me to help him as he was lost.
The stranger requested me to help him as he were lost.
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is option c)

Explanation:

•While changing the narration of an imperative sentence, we need to follow steps

•If the sentence is starting with "Please" and there is a request, we make the following changes-

•The reporting verb said is changed into requested or begged.

•Then 'to' infinitive with 1st form of the verb is used, followed the objective form of the pronoun. (Me-Him)

•The rest part is used as it is with the tense in past form.

Eventually, we will get the final sentence- "The stranger requested me to help him as he was lost."

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Remote work and flexible schedules have become more common, allowing employees to achieve a better work-life balance.

B. This shift has also opened up new opportunities for people with disabilities, caregivers, and those living in remote areas, promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workforce.

C. The future of work is evolving rapidly, influenced by technological advancements and changing workforce dynamics.

D. As a result, productivity and job satisfaction have increased, leading to improved overall well-being for workers.
questions.solution_en:
The correct order to form a coherent paragraph is CADB.

Sentence C introduces the topic by stating that "The future of work is evolving rapidly," setting the context for discussing changes in work dynamics.

Sentence A follows by detailing one specific change: "Remote work and flexible schedules have become more common, allowing employees to achieve a better work-life balance." This sentence builds on the theme of evolving work dynamics presented in C. Accordingly, CA forms a logical pair.

Sentence D then explains the positive outcomes of these changes: "As a result, productivity and job satisfaction have increased, leading to improved overall well-being for workers." This shows the effects of remote work and flexible schedules mentioned in A.

Sentence B concludes the paragraph by expanding on the implications of these changes, noting that this shift has opened up new opportunities for underrepresented groups, thus promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion. This ties back to the evolving nature of work while emphasising its broader social impact. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

She is looking forward to meet / her old school friends again / at the upcoming alumni event.
options_en: She is looking forward to meet
questions.solution_en:
The error is in the part "She is looking forward to meet". The phrase 'look forward to' is a phrasal verb. When a verb follows this phrase, it must be in the gerund form (verb + -ing). The 'to' in 'look forward to' is a preposition, not an infinitive marker. Prepositions are followed by nouns or gerunds.

Therefore, the infinitive 'meet' should be replaced by the gerund 'meeting'.

Correct Sentence: She is looking forward to meeting her old school friends again at the upcoming alumni event.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Note:

· Phrasal verb: A phrase that consists of a verb with a preposition or adverb or both, the meaning of which is different from the meaning of its separate parts. Example: She has always looked down on me. Here, the phrasal verb 'to look down on someone' doesn't mean that you are looking down from a higher place at someone who is below you; it means that you think that you are better than someone.

· Gerund: Gerund is a verb form that functions as a noun, ending in -ing. A gerund can be either the subject or object of a sentence in English. Example: "Everybody enjoyed her dancing and singing at the party." The words 'dancing' and 'singing' are gerunds.

questions.q_en: Select the correct sentence in active voice from the following options.
options_en: A delicious three-course meal will be prepared for the guests by his wife.
His wife prepared a delicious three-course meal for the guests.

A delicious three-course meal had been prepared for the guests by his wife.
questions.solution_en:
Option (b) is in the active voice. It contains the subject (his wife) performing the action (prepared). The emphasis of the sentence is on the doer of the action ('his wife').

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

Options (a) and (d) are in passive voice, focusing on what will happen to the meal rather than who is doing the preparation. The emphasis is on the receiver of the action ('a delicious three-course meal').

Option (c) is the construction of the sentence in direct speech. Here again, the emphasis is on the receiver of the action.

You taught by whom to play the keyboard this smoothly?
By whom you taught to play the keyboard this smoothly?
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. The object of the Active voice is changed into the subject of the Passive voice. The usage of a 'to be' form of the verb ['were' here] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The preposition "by" is used before the object made in passive voice.

The question in Active voice is in Interrogative form. This is "wh" question that doesn't take yes or no as the answer.

'Who' is changed into 'by whom'.

For example:

Who taught you Science? (Active voice)

By whom were you taught Science? (Passive voice)

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:

The ___________ of the worker was very loud when he found the ___________.
questions.solution_en:
Option (a) is the correct choice.

A roar is a loud, deep sound uttered by a person or crowd. An ore is a naturally occurring solid material from which a metal or valuable mineral can be extracted. The sentence is about the excitement of the worker when he found the mineral.

In the following questions, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.

Meenakshi will complete her project next week.
options_en: Next week her project will be completed by Meenakshi.
Her project will have to complete next week by Meenakshi.
Her project will being completed next week by Meenakshi.
Meenakshi’s project will be completing by her next week.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of active voice becomes the object in passive voice and vice-versa. Moreover, the subject and the object interchange their placements in the sentence in active and passive voices and third form of verb is used. Case of future indefinite tense: In passive voice, we use “Object+ will/shall + be + V3 + by + Subject”.

Among the given options, only option (a) follows the rules of passive voice. Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Navigating the labyrinthine corridors of / ancient history, historians unravels the complexities / of bygone civilizations, piecing together / narratives lost in the sands of time.
options_en: ancient history, historians unravels the complexities
narratives lost in the sands of time.
questions.solution_en:
The plural noun 'historians' needs to be followed by the plural verb 'unravel' or the past form verb 'unravelled' but not singular verb 'unravels'. Hence, option (b) is the answer.

The correct sentence is: Navigating the labyrinthine corridors of ancient history, historians unravel the complexities of bygone civilizations, piecing together narratives lost in the sands of time.

OR

Navigating the labyrinthine corridors of ancient history, historians unravelled the complexities of bygone civilizations, piecing together narratives lost in the sands of time.

questions.q_en:
Identify the pair of synonyms from the underlined words in the given sentence.

Being frugal with his money was a habit he learned early; this thrifty nature allowed him to save a significant sum, proving that careful planning can lead to long-term security.
questions.solution_en:
Option (a): "Habit" is a settled or regular tendency. "Save" means to keep and store up money for future use. They are not synonyms.

Option (b): "Significant" means sufficiently great or important to be worthy of attention. "Careful" means making sure of avoiding potential danger or errors. These are not synonyms.

Option (c): "Frugal" means sparing or economical with regard to money. "Thrifty" means using money and other resources carefully and not wastefully. Both words describe the practice of being careful with money, making them synonyms.

Option (d): "Long-term" means occurring over a long period of time. "Security" is the state of being free from danger or threat. They are not synonyms.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.
